flows.note: the gateway holds revocations in process memory, so API-02 asserts the panel says the revocation does not survive a restart and names the expiry that does; API-03 asserts an undelivered revocation never reads as a registered one

flows.name: The api-access developer console: OpenAPI explorer, token introspection, try-it, and the key-ceremony deep link into the host
flows.note: The console is a spec-073 registry package, so its surface only exists where a registry can be written to and package bytes can be served: the on-chain tier publishes api-access through publish:local:miniapps and launches it through the real submit/approve/launchable path, with only the IPFS transport and the member API stubbed (bodies copied from services/relay-gateway/src/memberApi/). API-06 reads the permission set out of the manifest the chain committed to — no wallet:submit, no contracts — and API-10 asserts the key ceremony lands on the HOST's api-access card — on Tools ▸ Assistant since spec 104, card id unchanged — because a package cannot sign. API-08 reads the app's store namespace back out of localStorage to prove the bearer token was never persisted. The unconfigured-gateway branch of the host card is NOT reachable from any e2e build (no dev server produces relayerBaseUrl() === ''), so it is held at unit level in frontend/src/test/ApiAccessPanel.test.jsx instead.

specs.title: x402 pay-per-request access to the member API
specs.reason: An agent-facing HTTP rail with no member surface: an unauthenticated caller is answered 402 with a price, pays with an X-PAYMENT header, and is served as the payer. No component, route or member journey changes, and a member holding a capability token never enters the path. Its gate is the gateway vitest suite (services/relay-gateway/test/x402.test.js) plus the spec-095 suites passing unchanged with the rail enabled, and node:test coverage of the MCP server's 402 surfacing and payment passthrough.

specs.title: Workstation secrets and local observability
specs.reason: Operator tooling with no member surface: credentials move off a local .env into Secret Manager and are delivered per least-privilege profile by a wrapper, and the Prometheus and Grafana stack is a read-only viewing surface bound to loopback. Nothing here is reachable from the app, and the workstation identity is declared Terraform with no service-account key file. Gated by the scripts/secrets vitest suites (including the registry/tfvars parity test, which fails on drift because a missing grant surfaces later as PERMISSION_DENIED), check:env-hygiene, and the Terraform plan.

The chain-mismatch reason is covered (APR-01), as is the negative that the refusal no longer applies to eligible kinds (APR-02 hardware, APR-03 same-chain vault). specs.title: GutterToken assistant rail and client-side tools

flows.name: Save a GutterToken key only when GutterToken accepts it, keep it when GutterToken cannot be reached, and remove it
flows.note: The key spends the member's OWN prepaid GutterToken credit, so the two save outcomes are asserted apart: a 401 refuses the save and stores nothing, while an unreachable GutterToken saves WITH the failure shown (spec 069's rule — a timeout is a fact about the network, not about the key). GT-01 then sweeps the DOM for the raw key and proves the only storage entry holding it is the wallet-scoped assistant_guttertoken_key_v1; GT-02 removes it and reads the absence back from storage, not from the card's own state.

flows.name: A non-member with a saved key gets an answer straight from GutterToken, with no request to the FairWins chat route
flows.note: SC-001, and the absence is the assertion: the gateway chat route is intercepted only so the spec can prove it received nothing, while the reply is served from the intercepted api.guttertokens.com POST. Membership answers tier 0 at the RPC transport, so the launcher is reached by the key alone.

flows.name: GutterToken's 403 and 429 each get their own sentence and action, and neither produces a reply bubble
flows.note: SC-002. An empty balance is the member's own money running out, so it names the balance and links to GutterToken billing; a 429 is GutterToken's per-network rate limit and carries the Retry-After it sent. Both are asserted with .assistant-panel__message--assistant absent — an invented reply is the one failure a member cannot detect.

flows.name: A paid member switches rails, and the badge and the transport agree about which one answered
flows.note: The badge is a claim about where the member's words went and who paid, so it is checked against the request counters on both endpoints rather than against itself: on GutterToken the gateway chat route stays at zero calls, and on FairWins api.guttertokens.com does.

flows.name: A tool round shows what is being read and reports a failed read as could not be read, never as zero
flows.note: The model asks for two reads in one round; the member API answers one and refuses the other. The refused one must render as 'could not be read' in both the live progress row and the Sources line — an unreadable chain is not an empty one, and the panel never gets to fill the gap with a zero.

flows.name: The agent controls live on Tools ▸ Assistant, Settings no longer carries them, and the old Settings hashes redirect
flows.note: SC-005. Both halves are asserted, because a tab that renders the cards while Settings still renders them too is two homes for one control: the redirect is read off the resolved URL, and the card lands OPEN rather than at a closed heading.

specs.title: Passkey account recovery — find the account, never guess it

flows.name: A member signing in on a new device reaches the account their passkey controls, including when that passkey was added to the account later rather than being the key that created it
flows.note: Blocked on T-101: accountFactory has no recorded deploy block on any chain, so a log scan has no floor -- and this repo degrades that silently (deployBlocks?.X || 0 starts at block 0) rather than loudly. Release 1 confirms a single derived candidate and reports none-found honestly for every other shape.

flows.name: A passkey whose account cannot be verified never opens a session on an unverified address; the member is told what could not be confirmed, and an unreachable chain reads as unverified rather than as no account existing
flows.note: The no-chain tier is the right home AND the natural one: it runs with no RPC reachable, which is exactly the condition that produces the unverified verdict, so the environment generates the state rather than a stub asserting it does. REC-01 pins the regression (no session row, header still offering connection); REC-02 pins that an unreachable network never reads as "you have no account".

flows.name: A member relinks by entering their account address, and is signed in only when the chain lists the recovered key among that account's current owners
flows.note: The member-facing half is covered without a chain: the form, the refusal of a malformed address in words rather than colour, and the address being handed on to be CHECKED rather than trusted. The half that needs a chain -- a real deployed account confirming the key and a session opening on it -- belongs to the full-stack passkey tier.
flows.missing: The chain agreeing. This tier reaches no RPC, so what is proven is the form, the refusal of a malformed address, and that the address is handed on to be CHECKED — never that a verified address opens a session on the account it names. That needs a deployed account whose owner set includes a key this browser has no record of, i.e. the full-stack passkey tier.

specs.title: Guided Multichain Vault Creation — One Vault, Chosen Networks

flows.name: A non-technical member walks the four-sheet flow (type presets, rules tile grid with live summary, cohort network multi-select) with every refusal stated in plain language and no network question before a signature needs one
The flow deploys the vault and the deployed address IS the predicted one, with per-network status reaching Live from a real receipt
flows.missing: deployment to a SECOND network in the same run (identical address, wallet switch mid-orchestration, per-network failure isolation) — the on-chain tier runs one private chain per leg, so the multi-network half is the staged manual protocol in docs/runbooks/multichain-vault-staging-validation.md (#1491); the state machine and CREATE2 identity across chainIds are Vitest-proven

flows.name: The chosen rules install on each network after deployment — directly where the creator alone meets the threshold, queued as awaiting-approval where co-owners must sign — and an over-cap send is refused by the realized policy
flows.note: CV-01 deliberately creates with rules OFF (it asserts the no-rules initializer stays byte-identical to spec 043); RL-01/RL-02 are the rules-ON legs — direct and queued installs read back from the guard's own getRules, and the lanes govern real transfers (banded-lane allow, big-send refusal on one approval, full-vote completion by the executing co-owner).

flows.name: A passkey member creates a governed vault in ONE sendCalls batch (deploy + both rule installs), landing at the predicted address with the record written from it — and a chain with no bundler states the write-rail reason on its chip instead of attempting the batch
flows.note: Runs only on the cypress-passkey-full-stack job (bundler + gateway). The batch is possible because the CREATE2 address is known before deployment; the vault, its guard slot and the realized lanes are read back from the chain, and the reference + creation record are asserted to carry the PREDICTED address, never one parsed from a receipt. The batch composition itself (every call addressed, one sendCalls) is pinned by useVaultDeployment.test.jsx.

flows.name: From Details, a vault with a creation record deploys to a cohort network it is not on yet at the SAME address; a drifted owner set is disclosed as the original arrangement first; a vault without a record gets the honest reason, never a dead control
flows.missing: the replay deployment itself and FR-019 already-live need a SECOND custody network, which the one-chain full tier cannot host — staged manual protocol (docs/runbooks/multichain-vault-staging-validation.md, #1491). The record gate is chain-proven: the record holder is OFFERED Deploy for the missing cohort network (RL-01) and the no-record co-owner gets the honest FR-018 reason (RL-02); gating, disclosure and orchestrator handoff stay Vitest/component-proven (VaultDetailsView.test.jsx).

flows.name: Details renders ONE card — compact network status rows, shared facts stated once with drift naming the differing network and coverage naming the unread one — never a repeated per-network card or an up-front switch gate

Queue chips (All / Needs you / per-network) filter the rows without touching the four-state per-chain read disclosure; recognised proposals read in plain language and unknown calldata keeps the honest raw row

specs.title: Gateway caller authentication
specs.reason: Gateway-side caller-identity tiers, quota re-keying and enforcement — server behaviour with no member surface of its own, covered by 34 gateway vitest files (test/identity/). The one member-visible artifact today is the invisible, silently-degrading Turnstile widget (aria-hidden until a surface opts into interactive escalation); member-facing flows arrive when a surface adopts it and when IDENTITY_ENFORCE changes refusal paths on the Predict/Collect/BTC write flows already rowed under specs 055-057/061.

specs.title: Keyed RPC access
specs.reason: Runtime-issued read-only RPC credentials. Dormant end to end until an issuance endpoint is configured (#1438 runbook); every client failure mode falls back to the public default the app uses today, so there is no member-distinguishable flow yet. Covered by gateway vitest (test/access.test.js) and frontend vitest (src/test/network/issuedAccess.test.js); a member-facing degradation-disclosure flow gets a row when the disclosure surface ships.

specs.title: Multi-currency wrap/unwrap — the asset is the entry point

flows.name: The Wrap view offers every cohort chain's base coin the member holds from one trading-view-style picker (icon, symbol, network, balance), with unreadable balances shown as unread (never zero) and unconfigured wrappers honestly absent
flows.note: WMC-02 pins null-not-zero for an unreadable chain and the switch disclosure; WMC-04 pins the refused-switch wording (both chains named, nothing sent) via the mock wallet's rejectChainSwitch.

flows.name: Selecting a coin whose chain differs from the wallet's switches the wallet at submit time (settle loop), wraps against that chain's own wrapped-native contract, and a refused switch names both chains and sends nothing
flows.note: The member signs something that costs money, so execution lives here (e2e policy rule 2). WXC-01 starts the mock wallet on Mordor and wraps the local chain's coin — the switch-then-settle path against a real deposit(), asserted by the wrapped balance read back from the chain; WXC-03 closes the 1:1 round trip.

specs.title: Token news on portfolio and trade surfaces

flows.name: Selecting a portfolio token shows that asset's latest news with link-out attribution; an unreadable feed renders a sentence + retry (never an empty feed pretending to be no news), an unmapped asset renders honest absence, and the module off hides the card
Selecting a trade pair shows the pair's token news below the amount entry under the same three-state honesty; items are text with attribution, never rendered HTML

specs.title: Seamless multichain UX — chain-abstracted writes on a single EVM seam

flows.name: With the wallet on network B, tapping Claim on a wager living on network A resolves the target chain from the wager, moves the wallet through the one switch-and-settle seam, and completes the claim as a real settled transaction — no in-app 'switch network' step
A wallet declining the network change signs nothing, and one message names both networks and what would fix it (spec 108 WXC-04 wording precedent, generalized to every write surface)

An acting identity whose rail cannot reach the target chain (passkey on bundlerless ETC/Mordor; vault signer elsewhere) sees the unavailability stated BEFORE the tap, naming the chain and the way out — never a submit-time chain-support error
A relayed EIP-712 intent targeting network A is signed while connected to network B with no network change requested at all — the chain lives in the signature domain
